trust_decision.summary: Whether a caller-supplied key string/buffer is an asymmetric PEM key/cert or a raw HMAC secret is decided by ^-anchored regexes on key.trim() in the two crypto.js detectors; a non-whitespace prefix makes a PEM public key classify as an HS secret, so its bytes become the HMAC key (createSecretKey) and HS256 tokens are accepted.

landing_point.why: The summary names RSA->HS256 confusion and an incomplete earlier whitespace (trim) fix; the verifier-side detector performDetectPublicKeyAlgorithms opens with key.trim() and the ^-anchored publicKeyPemMatcher.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about verifier-side RSA->HS256 forgery; the signer only uses keys the application owns, so a solver can argue the private-key detector (public key misused as a signing secret) is a neighbouring hardening, not the vulnerability.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Raw HMAC secrets that are arbitrary text must still classify as HS; a verifier with an HS-only algorithms allowlist deliberately treats PEM-looking strings as raw secrets; prefixed but valid PEMs (comment or 'Bag Attributes' lines before the header) must still be detected as RS/ES/EdDSA, not rejected outright.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A planted key-normalisation helper (e.g. strip a leading BOM or label line) applied before prepareKeyOrSecret but after detection, so classification and key material disagree.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Maintainers have repeatedly patched key-format leniency in this lineage; a 'tolerate BOM/headers' convenience is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An async key-callback path that runs its own lightweight isPem check instead of detectPublicKeyAlgorithms (a second implementation at distance in our copy).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The async path already differs from the sync one (no allowlist passed at src/verifier.js:456, [0]=== vs includes at src/verifier.js:464 vs src/verifier.js:524).

O9_family: CWE-347 signature verification bypass via key-type misclassification (parser differential between JS regex classifier and OpenSSL PEM reader)
